labels.disclaimer: AI guidance only. This is not a final diagnosis. Please consult a qualified doctor for medical advice and prescription.

topics.chest: a possible serious chest, heart, or blood pressure related concern
topics.breathing: a possible breathing, asthma, chest infection, or respiratory concern
topics.fever: a possible viral fever, flu-like illness, COVID-like illness, or throat infection
topics.stomach: a possible stomach infection, food poisoning, acidity, or digestive upset
topics.headache: a possible migraine, tension headache, sinus headache, BP-related headache, or neurological concern
topics.skin: a possible skin allergy, rash, eczema, infection, or reaction
topics.urine: a possible urinary tract infection, kidney irritation, or stone-related concern
topics.sugar: a possible blood sugar imbalance or diabetes-related concern
topics.women: a possible gynecology or women’s health concern
topics.child: a child health concern requiring pediatric review
topics.eye: a possible eye infection, allergy, strain, injury, or vision concern
topics.bone: a possible muscle strain, joint inflammation, injury, sprain, or orthopedic concern
topics.mental: a possible anxiety, panic, stress, sleep difficulty, or mood concern

tests.ecg: ECG, blood pressure, pulse, oxygen saturation, and urgent doctor review if active.
tests.oxygen: Oxygen saturation, chest examination, and chest X-ray if fever or congestion is present.
tests.fever: Temperature record, CBC if fever continues beyond 2–3 days, and flu/COVID test if needed.
tests.stomach: Hydration check, stool test if severe, CBC/electrolytes if weak, and ultrasound if localized pain is severe.
tests.headache: Blood pressure check, eye/vision check, and neurology review if severe, new, or recurrent.
tests.skin: Skin examination, allergy history, and skin test/culture if infection is suspected.
tests.urine: Urine routine examination, urine culture if recurrent, and kidney ultrasound if flank pain is present.
tests.sugar: Fasting sugar, random sugar, HbA1c, and ketone check if sugar is very high with vomiting.
tests.bp: Repeat BP after rest, pulse check, ECG if chest discomfort exists, and labs if doctor advises.
tests.women: Pregnancy test if possible, CBC for heavy bleeding, pelvic ultrasound if pain or irregular bleeding continues.
tests.child: Pediatric examination, temperature record, urine test if fever source is unclear, and CBC if child looks unwell.
tests.eye: Eye examination, vision check, and corneal exam if injury or contact lens pain is present.
tests.bone: Physical examination, X-ray if injury/deformity exists, and MRI only if nerve signs are present.
tests.mental: Basic medical review if symptoms are new and mental health screening if symptoms continue.
tests.general: Basic vitals check and doctor-guided tests only if symptoms continue.

en.base: This analysis is written only in the selected language and matched to the symptom category. Duration, severity, age, and warning signs can change the risk level.
en.rec2: Monitor symptom duration, severity, triggers, and any worsening. Book a doctor consultation if symptoms continue or affect routine activity.
en.medicine: Medicine names and doses are disabled for safety. A qualified doctor or pharmacist should confirm any medicine, dose, and duration.
en.red: Seek urgent care if symptoms are severe, rapidly worsening, or include chest pain, breathing difficulty, fainting, confusion, severe bleeding, seizure, or severe dehydration.
en.unclear: Please write a clear symptom such as fever with cough, stomach pain with vomiting, chest pain, burning urine, or rash with itching.
